utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge El Mahdi. I just have a few questions to ask you by myself. Did you see the dead body of your father, your grandfather, and your grandmother on the 9th of September, that day?
No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Do you know how many BiH soldiers are there present in that village on that day?
I saw three buses of them, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So approximately 100, 150?
Perhaps others arrived later, but that's what I can remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. At this stage, are there any questions out of Judges' questions? Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Morrissey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Are there any documents to tender at this moment from both parties? I see none. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. The usher will show you out of the room when she pulls down the blinds. We all wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, since we still have 30 minutes left, I believe that we should make the best use of this time. And there's some procedural questions I would like to ask the parties. The first one is about the Prosecution's witness list. Mr. Weiner, would you please inform me that how many witnesses we are going to hear this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We've heard the first, and then two more. One should be another single-day witness, and then the third witness will be a longer witness. A number of documents will be introduced through that witness, and he'll be discussing a large number. And counsel indicated that there would be more extensive cross-examination, so that witness could drag into Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. I think we should make the best use of time and try to finish that witness within this week, we hope. Yes. As for the second witness on your list for the next week, we understand that witness is a 92 bis witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That witness is currently on the 92 bis list, but there has been no decision made as to whether or not he is in fact a 92 bis witness. And unless a decision is made, we would probably call him live.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. I see there's no objections from the Defence side to regard that witness as a 92 bis witness, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, in relation to that witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The second witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- yes, Your Honour. We are awaiting the decision in relation to him. We hadn't thought to object because we were awaiting that decision. But he is a witness of -- who we would wish to cross-examine. No matter what occurs, we would wish to cross-examine him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You wish to cross-examine this witness. Well, is it possible we treat this witness as a 92 bis witness with cross-examination? Which means that the direct examination will be extremely short, only admit his statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: As we told the Court, we were hoping to do more witnesses either under 92 bis or 89(F) to move a number of witnesses through, and that would be fine, if we could put together a statement and talk to him -- finalise a statement on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Thank you very much. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, might by heard on that matter? We understand what the Court said at an earlier stage to encourage the Prosecution to take that course. There are some witnesses that we would wish to object to that course being taken. The second, third, and sixth witnesses on the list before you are all witnesses from the 9th Brigade, are all controversial, and all feature in -- heavily in the case against Mr. Halilovic in terms of notice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid that we are not talking about the same list. The list I'm using is their filings from the Prosecution on the 1st of February, 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That will be the witness list for the next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I believe I have -- I hope I have the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I think the problem is, Your Honour, he -- the witness was originally a 92 bis witness but was moved onto the regular list, moved onto the live witness list. But we could try and probably do him maybe under 89(F) or 92 bis, if we could move quick enough and get enough information. Maybe get additional information and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: -- see what we could do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is the area of controversy, and it may be appropriate to hear a submission about it at another time or now, or we could reduce it to writing, if that would assist the Court. But with respect to -- to the witnesses I indicated, we would want to make a submission against them being dealt with in any way under 89 or under 92 bis. They are witnesses about whom there will be controversy, to use the most neutral term available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Maybe we could find another time to deal with this issue in details.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, he seems to go to the acts of the accused in -- which is the main part of his testimony. But it seems to be a witness of very limited testimony; mainly in relation to certain acts of the accused. So it's -- we're not talking about an extensive direct examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No. Yes, I think, you know, you make your own strategy concerning with the witnesses, you know. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The next issue is about the proofing notes. We received proofing notes which is about five or six pages. I believe that, you know, the Prosecution misunderstood the intention of this Bench, and later on I believe that I only need one piece of paper which only listed whatever the witness summary does not include. Which means that we already have the summaries of the testimony of this witness already, but when this witness comes to The Hague, he might say something which is out of scope of that summary or changed his previous statement. We only want an indication of that but not on that extensive, you know, scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the total proofing notes, there's three pages, but they're really two -- a total of two pages. What happened is when they were given in discovery, they -- they stapled proofing notes for two different witnesses. So it's not a total of five pages. One is really two pages and the other is pretty much two pages too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, our intention is to reduce the paper as much as possible because we have been flooded with all the motions and the papers already. The last issue is about a new motion filed by the Prosecution and ask for the leave to disclose about 14 documents under Rule 68 to the Defence. Are you ready to discuss this issue? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. So I understand that those documents are all in the B/C/S, not translated into English yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. As I understand from the Rules, the Prosecution does not have to translate documents that are disclosable under Rule 68, but we will endeavour, of course, to do that if you require us to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that may be a big problem, you know. Let's hear Mr. Morrissey, you know, about that. Or Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good evening, Your Honour. Yes, as my learned colleague from the Prosecution pointed out, the Rules don't provide for a specific requirement for translation, but indeed as underlined by the Prosecution and by yourself it is not very helpful for counsel in this case to receive material in the Bosnian -- or B/C/S language, as neither of us speak that language. We'd be very grateful indeed to the Prosecution if we could be provided those documents in English and as soon as possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution can endeavour to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I hope, you know, any documents disclosed to the other side could be translated into a language that the other party could understand, taking into the consideration that this case may be very short and those documents are 68 materials which might prove that the accused is innocent. I haven't, you know, looked at those documents yet, but I think we should do everything possible to disclose any materials that is favourable to the accused. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Another brief matter, Your Honour: On the face of it, those documents appear to be relevant as a minimum and of potential great importance if they are what they appear to be. And the Defence would move to ask that witnesses to whom those documents could relate should not be called by the Prosecution until that time when we have been able to review all of those documents fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, those documents are 68 documents. Any response from the Prosecution side? Which means that are you going to use this document in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: No. The Prosecution has no intention of using these documents, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. So we'll make a decision as soon as possible for the disclosure of those documents. Is there anything else that the parties would like to bring to the attention to this Bench?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's one other matter that I would seek to raise. The evidence of the witness just passed throws it into sharp relief. That witness was in a position to give evidence about the individual Celo, Ramiz Delalic. The nature of the cross-examination of that witness proceeded in a state of anxious uncertainty as to whether that witness, Mr. Delalic, will in fact appear. I didn't raise it as an objection because I saw fit to proceed, and I -- that's my decision. But it is a matter that may arise in a focussed form with other witnesses who are coming soon; in particular, the witnesses indicated on the witness list for next week. It's for the Tribunal to make its own schedule as to delivering those rulings, of course. But I just put on record that it creates some dilemmas for the Defence as to whether that man is -- whether that witness is to be called -- permitted to be called as a witness because the structure of cross-examination may change in relation to these other witnesses, depending upon the outcome of that. In other words, we may be compelled to put certain matters to those witnesses. So I raise that as an issue that's troubling the Defence. I understand that all is being done that can be done. But it is -- it is a live issue for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll do our best to deliver any rulings as soon as possible, as soon as possible. Yes. And another issue is about video conference link. I've been advised by the registrar that on the 9th and 10th of February we'll have the video conference link. So we might stop the testimony of a witness in the middle which we did not want to see that. So I hope maybe there's some rearrangement of the witnesses, because those two days are set. They must testify on that two days. If there's any changes of order of the witnesses the Prosecution would like to call, I hope we could be informed as early as possible as well as to the other party, the Defence. Well, having said that, I believe that we'll adjourn until tomorrow afternoon, 2.15 as usual.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 2nd day of February, 2005, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.43 p.m.,
